researchQuestions: RQ1: Does the presence and content of controlled verification-related history change candidate policy scope and observable future actions in a direction-appropriate way (C-E)?
RQ2: Do irrelevant history changes (EN) leave decisions stable (drift control)?
RQ3: When reliable counter-evidence arrives, does the agent revise locally while retaining correct behavior in untouched old contexts (plasticity + stability)?
theme: dynamic trade-off between verification sufficiency and efficiency
themeQuestion: How does one choose the minimally sufficient discriminating verification under evidence uncertainty, check cost, failure risk, task deadline and owner authorization?

evidenceRefs.claim: EA world: hidden dynamic consumer breakage with high loss; a cheap targeted check was discriminative
EB world: current credible contract harness made exhaustive re-verification net-negative (missed hotfix deadline)
Owner correction reinforcing targeted-check practice in the EA world
Owner correction reinforcing contract-reliance in the EB world

assumptions: Verification sufficiency decisions recur in this synthetic world family.
Both over-verification and under-verification have measurable costs in the fixture.
initialDecision.note: Conditional research suggestion only (SPEC v0.3 §3.2); not a production necessity truth.
